statusDetail: Coverage-complete report-mode audit of eight representative routes/templates and conditions.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page site with custom Apple global navigation and template JavaScript
page.notes: Public marketing, product, accessibility, search, error, internationalised, and commerce-entry surfaces. Not covered: authenticated account management, payment submission, order completion, and post-purchase support because they require credentials, personal data, or a real transaction.

paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, representing the primary marketing entry and shared global chrome.
iPhone category listing, representing a product-family index and comparison entry.
iPhone 17 Pro detail page, representing an immersive product narrative with scroll-driven presentation.
Buy iPhone 17 Pro configurator entry, representing the primary commerce journey through model selection.
Site search empty-result state, representing search and recoverable empty-state handling.
Unknown route, representing HTTP failure messaging and recovery navigation.
Accessibility landing page, representing a media-rich editorial/values template.
Arabic UAE homepage, representing right-to-left localisation and internationalised navigation.

findings.summary: The public marketing surface does not follow the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, matchMedia returned true but the root color-scheme remained normal and the body stayed rgb(255,255,255) with rgb(29,29,31) text. The dark-condition screenshot is visually the same light surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map shared surfaces and text tokens through light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme media query, while preserving intentional dark product sections.

findings.summary: Cross-document product navigation does not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Live CSS inspection across 1,789,564 bytes on the product detail page found zero view-transition rules, while category-to-detail navigation is a prominent state change.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } for same-origin category-to-product navigation, use stable view-transition-name values on shared product identity, and retain a non-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Overlay positioning uses custom modal plumbing rather than CSS anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: The product CSS probe found zero anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try rules and counted 35 custom role=dialog/aria-modal surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: For non-modal menus, help bubbles, and anchored disclosures, progressively adopt popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks so controls stay attached at viewport edges.

findings.summary: Rich overlays are implemented as custom ARIA modal structures instead of native dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM inspection found 35 custom role=dialog/aria-modal surfaces but zero dialog, popover, or details elements on the product page; the homepage global flyout is also custom div chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows, popover for transient menus and help, and details for disclosures where semantics fit. Keep ARIA only for names and relationships not supplied by the native primitive.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-driven rather than component-driven.
findings.evidence: Live CSS inspection found zero @container rules across 1,789,564 bytes of product-page CSS, despite reusable cards, galleries, local navigation, and commerce modules appearing in multiple widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable modules an inline-size query container and move local adaptations to @container rules, retaining viewport queries only for page-level composition.

findings.summary: Lab Core Web Vitals are outside the good range on key templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 11.7 s and CLS 0.166 on the homepage. First-party mobile layout capture measured CLS 0.194 on the product detail page and 0.282 on the accessibility page.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile each LCP element, make it discoverable in initial HTML, prioritise it with fetchpriority/preload where warranted, and reserve all late media and banner geometry before paint.

findings.summary: Late content causes substantial layout shift on representative pages.
findings.evidence: The layout observer recorded CLS 0.282 on /accessibility/ and 0.194 on /iphone-17-pro/, both above the good threshold of 0.1, with shifts beginning around 1.5 to 3.4 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve media and dynamic module dimensions with width/height or aspect-ratio, match fallback font metrics, and avoid inserting locale or promotion chrome above existing content.

findings.summary: The critical path carries a large font payload and many parser-blocking stylesheets.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 2.32 MB transferred, including 1.18 MB across seven fonts. It identified nine parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets as render-blocking candidates; Lighthouse’s 11.7 s LCP corroborates delayed delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset and consolidate fonts, preload only the critical face, reduce critical CSS to the first viewport, and load route or gallery styles after critical rendering.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 117 KiB unused JavaScript and 40 KiB unused CSS. The main home bundle was 83.8% unused in the trace window and several stylesheets were 81% to 92% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Split global header, analytics, gallery, and page modules by interaction or template; defer optional modules until needed and extract only above-the-fold CSS into the initial path.

findings.summary: Entertainment-gallery action labels fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found action labels with contrast ratios from 1.64:1 to 2.5:1, including “Stream now”, “Play now”, and “Listen now”, below the required 4.5:1 for the rendered text sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply an opaque or reliably contrast-controlled label surface and choose text colors that maintain at least 4.5:1 against every gallery artwork state.

findings.summary: Image elements omit intrinsic dimensions across the homepage.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all 47 img elements lacked width and height attributes. Although the homepage layout sample was stable, other templates recorded CLS above 0.19, so relying on CSS and late image state is fragile.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width and height for every img and preserve responsive behavior with height:auto and appropriate picture/srcset sources.

findings.summary: Repeated generic link labels weaken page comprehension and search context.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported eight non-descriptive links: seven “Learn more” labels across different products and one “here” terms link. The destinations are crawlable, but the link text has little standalone meaning.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each link a specific accessible and visible label such as “Learn more about iPhone 17” and replace “here” with the destination or action.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but cookie and CSP settings leave avoidable exposure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found a CSP that allows both unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. Cookie inspection found the geo cookie lacked Secure and all six cookies used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval, migrate inline code and styles to nonces or hashes, mark every HTTPS cookie Secure, and use Lax or Strict unless a documented cross-site flow requires None.

findings.summary: Analytics collection begins on first load before an explicit privacy choice.
findings.evidence: The HAR and tracker probe recorded two securemetrics.apple.com requests and first-load analytics cookies including s_vi/s_fid. The metrics request included a visitor identifier, page, locale, currency, screen, and viewport fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the minimum event payload, shorten or avoid persistent identifiers, batch low-priority analytics, and gate non-essential measurement behind the applicable user choice and regional policy.

findings.summary: Defensive response policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: HSTS, nosniff, and X-Frame-Options are present, but Permissions-Policy is absent and Referrer-Policy remains no-referrer-when-downgrade rather than a stricter modern policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and use strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter. Prefer CSP frame-ancestors alongside X-Frame-Options and evaluate Trusted Types for script-heavy surfaces.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses modern format, lazy-loading, and intrinsic-size opportunities.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 47 legacy PNG/JPEG images, no modern-format img sources, 29 below-fold images without loading=lazy, 23 without srcset on the img element, and 47 without intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP through picture with JPEG fallback, emit responsive srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold media, and include intrinsic dimensions. Preserve eager/high priority only for the actual LCP image.

findings.summary: The first-view resource budget is high for a marketing landing page.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 2.32 MB in 51 requests before broad page exploration, dominated by 1.18 MB of fonts and 513 KB of images. The page also initializes analytics and media resources during load.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a first-view byte budget, subset fonts, defer below-fold gallery media and analytics work, and load only the hero variant needed for the current viewport and preference state.

taskList.title: Fix LCP and reserve late content geometry
Meet contrast requirements in entertainment gallery
Harden CSP, cookies, and browser policies
Reduce critical font, CSS, and JavaScript delivery
Replace custom overlay plumbing with native primitives
Respect the user’s dark color-scheme preference
